units.translation: Hesychius αἰγίζειν [to tear apart]: διασπᾶν [to tear apart], by metaphor, from which also αἰγίζεσθαι [to be storm-tossed] from καταιγίδων [squalls]. Aeschylus. The same author in the Edonians (fr. 60) also calls the fawn-skins thus. These words are partly read also in Suidas, on which see the annotation. Hermann conjectured that these were the poet's words. The words οὕτω λέγει [calls them thus] (καλεῖ [calls] in Suidas) seem to mean that the fawn-skins were called αἰγίδας [goat-skins] by Aeschylus.
and they tore apart the Edonian fawn-skins

It appears from these that the tenses of this verb are formed partly from αἰδοῦμαι [I feel shame] and partly from αἴδομαι [I feel shame]. However, the tragedians did not use the present participle αἰδόμενος [feeling shame] for αἰδούμενος [feeling shame] except when the meter required it, as Eum. 549 ἐπιστροφὰς δωμάτων αιδόμενός τις ἔστω [let someone be in awe of the turns of the house]. Suppl. 362 ποτιτρόπαιον αἰδόμενος [revering the suppliant]. Wellauer wanted to restore ἠδέσω [you felt shame] for ἠρκέσω [you kept away] at Eum. 213, on which passage see under ἥκω [I have come].
